subject: BlueJar dedicated: session topology, token mix & fleet deltas
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@bluejar.ai>, Kevin Ramos <kevin.ramos@bluejar.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueJar dedicated: session topology, token mix & fleet deltas

Hi Emma / Kevin —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. To get the dedicated sizing work started I attached a lightweight intake (bluejar_token_profile.csv) with a few sample rows and a short prompt corpus (prompt_samples.txt). Before we run simulation passes Marissa/Vivek will need clarity on three things so our estimator reflects realistic tail behavior: 

1) Traffic shape: do you expect a single sustained concurrency band (e.g., 200 sessions steady-state) or multi-modal windows (e.g., 50k short bursts around marketing triggers)? If you have any day/hour percentiles that helps.

2) Session pattern and KV-cache reuse: are sessions largely short-lived single-turn (webhook-style) or long-lived chat sessions that reuse a KV cache across turns? If chat, average turns per session and typical prefix length.

3) Latency SLO weightings: is p50 the main metric (interactive chat) or p99 (financial/legal workloads)? We map SLOs to oversubscription guards differently.

What I attached is intentionally sparse — if you can return the CSV with a couple of rows populated (typical prompt tokens, average response tokens, frequency) we'll run a baseline occupancy pass and follow up with a short readout.

Next step: if useful we can do a 30-minute sizing workshop (Marissa + Vivek + BlueJar infra) early next week — tell me a couple of windows that work.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bluejar_token_profile.csv (CSV stub, columns: session_type, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, avg_turns, sessions_per_min), prompt_samples.txt
From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@bluejar.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Ramos <kevin.ramos@bluejar.ai>, procurement@bluejar.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueJar dedicated: session topology, token mix & fleet deltas

Diego / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached a filled row in the CSV you sent back (we recreated as bluejar_token_profile.csv) and a few more example prompts. High level answers inline: 

- Traffic shape: mostly steady daytime traffic across US hours (0800-2000 PT) with two predictable spikes around product releases. Baseline concurrent sessions ~1,800 (long polling API), short spikes up to ~6,500 for ~10–15 minutes when pipelines finish.
- Session pattern: mix — 75% are single-turn inference (API call -> response), 25% are multi-turn chat (avg 6 turns, reuse KV cache). Prefixes for chat average 180 tokens, with 70 tokens per subsequent user turn.
- Latency SLO: interactive product teams care about p50 ~80–120ms; financial reporting has some p99 requirements but we can accept graceful fallback to lower-capacity model variants during extreme spikes.

We'd like a conservative estimate that shows both (A) capacity to meet p50 target at baseline and (B) cost/latency tradeoff for a cheaper oversubscription plan that can handle spikes with fallbacks.

Also looping in procurement for commercial constraints. Can we schedule the workshop Tuesday 9/3 or Wednesday 9/4 morning PT?

Emma Lin
Head of Infrastructure
BlueJar Analytics

Attachments referenced: bluejar_token_profile.csv (completed), prompt_samples.txt (5 canonical prompts)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@bluejar.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueJar dedicated: session topology, token mix & fleet deltas

Emma —

Thanks for the details — this is great. Quick notes on what we'll run and what we need from you before the workshop: 

Planned simulation passes:
- Occupancy baseline: model-run with your single-turn mix to estimate GPU occupancy and expected token-per-second throughput at baseline concurrency (1,800).
- Burst simulation: short-window spikes (6,500 sessions for 10/15min) to measure tail latency and queueing under different oversubscription factors.
- Cache-aware pass: multi-turn chat simulation to measure KV reuse savings and p99 delta when using session-affinity (1% of chat sessions reused vs 50% reuse scenarios).

What we need from BlueJar before the workshop (if available):
- Sample production logs (anonymized) showing per-minute session counts for a 7-day period OR a simple day/hour percentile breakdown.
- A single example of a "long chat" session (full turn list) in plain text to calibrate KV-cache prefix length.
- Any regulatory constraints on data residency (if certain requests must be routed to specific regions).

I'll run an initial quick-pass with what you provided and have an initial slide (model_mix_estimate.xlsx) ready by EOD Monday. Vivek — can you seed the baseline model-mix (gpt-XX style) and run an occupancy heuristic?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment planned: redwood_model_mix_estimate.xlsx (will include model choices and cost sensitivity per 100M tokens)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Emma Lin <emma.lin@bluejar.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueJar dedicated: session topology, token mix & fleet deltas

Marissa / Emma —

Quick run results from the lightweight pass (notes):

- Baseline occupancy (1,800 concurrent, mixed model_mix_estimate): estimated sustained GPU occupancy per A100-equivalent is ~58% with continuous batching enabled and prefix caching for chat sessions. This maps to ~22 A100-equivalent GPUs to meet p50 target at baseline with a 10% buffer.
- Burst headroom: to hit the 6,500 short spike with p99 < 3s without fallbacks we'd need to reserve ~68 A100-equivalent GPUs (uncommitted burst). If instead BlueJar accepts model-variant fallback (lower-capacity model for non-critical calls), we can cover spikes with 38 GPUs plus rapid autoscale and routing rules.
- KV-cache savings: if chat prefix reuse >40% observed, we anticipate a 12–18% reduction in token processing cost and 7–12% lower GPU occupancy.

I'll prepare two slides showing: (A) baseline committed footprint + cost at current committed pricing, (B) burst strategy with fallback and incremental cost. Also will add sensitivity to average response tokens (we assumed 200; if response dips to 120 tokens occupancy drops ~18%).

Next: workshop scheduled Wednesday 9/4 09:00 PT? Emma — confirm and send a calendar invite. Diego / Marissa I'll upload the initial estimate to the Drive link and share the HubSpot record.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Staff Engineer, Inference Optimization

References: preliminary results uploaded to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_bluejar-sizing (filename: redwood_model_mix_estimate.xlsx)

Vivek / team —

Wednesday 9/4 09:00 PT works — invite sent. Quick notes after skim of the initial sheet:

- The 22 GPU baseline looks in-line with our expectations but procurement will want a clear cost delta between (1) 22 reserved GPUs with 20% burst pool and (2) a 38-GPU committed plan that handles most spikes without fallbacks. Please include annualized cost, estimated token unit cost, and an SLA note about p99 behavior for the two options.
- For KV reuse: we'll try to produce a small anonymized sample of chat sessions today for the cache pass.
- Compliance: all BlueJar EU customer data must remain in eu-west-1; not relevant to this US sizing pass but flagging for later private deployment discussion.

See you on the call.

Emma Lin
